payload.raw: StreamMDX treats MDX as an opt-in feature. Plain Markdown streams fast and predictably. MDX adds custom components, but requires compilation. You can enable it only where you need it:

payload.raw: MDX component registry

inline.text: MDX component registry

payload.raw: MDX components are passed separately from block overrides:

inline.text: MDX components are passed separately from block overrides:

payload.highlightedHtml:
const mdxComponents = {
  Callout: ({ title, children }: { title: string; children: React.ReactNode }) => (
    <div className="rounded border border-border p-4">
      <div className="font-semibold">{title}</div>
      <div className="mt-2">{children}</div>
    </div>
  ),
};

<StreamingMarkdown text={content} mdxComponents={mdxComponents} />

payload.raw: HTML blocks

inline.text: HTML blocks

payload.raw: When HTML is enabled, raw HTML blocks are sanitized and rendered with a configurable allowlist. You can also swap HTML tags for your own components:

inline.text: When HTML is enabled, raw HTML blocks are sanitized and rendered with a configurable allowlist. You can also swap HTML tags for your own components:

payload.highlightedHtml:
const htmlElements = {
  blockquote: ({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) => (
    <blockquote className="border-l-2 border-border pl-4 text-muted-old">{children}</blockquote>
  ),
};

<StreamingMarkdown text={content} htmlElements={htmlElements} features={{ html: true }} />

inline.text: When to use each feature

payload.raw:
- **Markdown only**: most content, best performance
- **HTML**: when you need raw HTML tags (tables, custom spans)
- **MDX**: when you need React components in content
